content: Diphenyl oxalate, commercially known as Cyalume, is a liquid ester that plays a critical role in the chemiluminescence observed in glow sticks. The light emission occurs as a result of the oxidation products of this compound. Diphenyl oxalate can be synthesized through the complete esterification of phenol with oxalic acid. Using derivatives such as salicylic acid in the synthesis process can result in the production of a brighter light. The 2,4,6-trichlorophenol ester of oxalic acid exists as a solid, which makes it more convenient to handle compared to its liquid counterparts. Additionally, trichlorophenolate serves as a superior leaving group in chemical reactions, allowing the reaction to proceed at a faster rate. This increased reaction efficiency also leads to the generation of a brighter light when compared to the phenol ester.
